headline: A hot CPI briefly pushed October hike odds to ~40% and $331M was liquidated in 24h, mostly longs; ETFs took in a provisional $176M on 10/13, but macro pressure drowned out the return of inflows.
summary: After September CPI beat forecasts, the 10-year yield spiked to 5.33% intraday before closing at 5.19%, the Nasdaq fell 1.9%, and BTC closed near the bottom of its daily range, back near the 50-day MA. Yet ETFs logged October's second-largest inflow on 10/13 and weighted funding rose to 7.71%, so flows are actually improving. The market stage stays Bull (day 6), and no exit-framework rule has fired or is close. Next: tonight's PPI (Taipei 20:30, 12:30 UTC) and the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

overview.lead: Bull day 6: a hot CPI pushed price back to the 50-day MA, but ETF inflows returned, funding rose, and valuation is still mid-cycle, so all three views say hold, no action.
points: Market stage: Bull (since 10/09); 35 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.556 (prior 0.547), 37.5% below the on-chain sell line (CoinMetrics 10/13).
Power-law multiple 0.581 (10/13): above the historical bottom band 0.24–0.48, below fair value 143,127.
Tidemark top signal 0, bottom signal 22.5: no signal either way (price date 10/13, not stale).

cycle.lead: Market stage: Bull (since 2026-10-09, day 6); 35 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA (threshold 30).
points: 200-day MA 72,204, above 70,191 thirty days ago and still rising; capitulation has occurred (2026-06-30, 58,525).

Supporting lights 3/6 (a sixth light was added on 10/14; they show strength of evidence only and do not decide the stage). Lit: MVRV above its 1-year mean (1.544 vs 1.439), realized cap +1.28% over 30 days, close above the short-term holder cost of 74,338 (10/08). Unlit: 12-month momentum (−27.9%), exchange supply over 90 days (+0.47%), short-term holder cost vs true market mean (−6.19%, 10/08).

Readings: extrapolating the last 30 days linearly, short-term holder cost would cross above the true market mean around 12/13. If price stays flat, 12-month momentum would turn positive around 2027-01-31. Both are assumptions, not forecasts.
Under the rules, Bull reverts to Bear only after 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; the current run below it is 0 days. Tidemark low test: no break of 58,525 before 12/19.

market.lead: After CPI, BTC closed at 9% of its daily range, below the value area and just above the 50-day MA: still a range, leaning weak.
points: Intraday 81,333–84,049; volume 1.12× the 20-day average and 0.90× the prior day; VWAP 82,506, above the close.
Value area 82,500–85,500, point of control 83,750; the close fell back below the value area. 20-day range position 0.0% (prior 29.4%).
The 20-day MA (83,802) is about 2.7% above and the 50-day MA (81,164) 0.5% below; Mayer multiple 1.130.
The up-leg that began 6/30 is 106 days old and up 39.4%; price is −5.8% from the leg high of 86,594, and the leg-end line of 73,605 is 9.8% below (reading only).

deriv.lead: Price fell while leverage came back: weighted funding rose to 7.71%, hedging demand eased slightly, and CPI-day liquidations were mostly longs. Leverage is still not heavy.
points: Three-venue weighted funding 7.71% annualized (prior 2.67%): Hyperliquid 10.95%, Deribit 6.46%, OKX 3.98%, all positive.
30-day 25Δ risk reversal −2.65 (prior −2.98), puts 38.96 vs calls 36.32; DVOL 39.12, 33.2th percentile over one year; median futures basis 5.61%.
10/16 weekly options: max pain 83,000, 4.4% of OI. 10/30: 37.2% of OI, max pain 79,000. 12/25: 33.0% of OI, max pain 75,000.

Order book (10/15 00:06 UTC, mid 81,711): within ±10%, bids $838M vs asks $552M. Hyperliquid perp bid walls at 81,000 (~$303M) and 80,000 (~$117M); ask wall at 82,000 (~$164M). Orders can be pulled at any time; reading only.

flows.lead: ETFs finally turned to inflows and new capital is still entering, but US spot demand is soft and rate pressure is back: flows move from weak to neutral.
points: Latest complete ETF day: 10/12, −$65.4M (The Block); the seven trading days 10/02–10/12 total −$556.7M. 10/13 provisional +$175.7M (Farside and SoSoValue agree; FBTC led with $103.1M).
US 10-year yield 5.21%, real yield 2.88%, +28 bp over 20 observations (FRED 10/13). After the 10/14 CPI it hit 5.33% intraday and closed at 5.19% (Reuters).
Realized cap +1.28% over 30 days (10/13), so capital is still flowing in. Stablecoin supply $306.1B: +0.85% over 30 days, −0.58% over 7.
Coinbase premium −0.142% (7-day avg −0.107%): US demand is soft. Fear & Greed 62 (71 a week ago). BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation 0.671 (10/13).

onchain.lead: Tuesday's bounce lifted the share of short-term holders in profit, but exchange supply rose 0.6% on the week and whale cohorts were mixed. The structure is unchanged.
points: Short-term holders in profit: 73.68% (10/13, prior 68.18%). Their cost basis of 74,338 (10/08) is about 8.9% below price.
Long-term holders net −78.2K BTC over 30 days (10/12, flat vs prior). Exchange supply: +0.6% over 7 days, −1.18% over 30, +0.47% over 90 (10/13).
The current 80–82K bucket holds 312K BTC. Above, 82–84K (841K) and 84–86K (1.23M) are overhead supply; below, 76–78K holds 556K BTC (URPD 10/13).

Whales: 100–1K cohort +35.4K BTC over 30 days, +113.5K since the leg began; 1K–10K +42.8K over 30 days but −9.5K over 7. Hash Ribbons show no capitulation (49 days); difficulty estimate +6.0% (10/16).

exit.lead: Exit framework: 0 rules fired today and none is close. Puell rebounded to 68.5, but all three top indicators remain below 75.
points: Price ladder: 8 steps of 12.5% each from 125K; step 1 is 53.2% away.
On-chain MVRV ratio 0.556; runs at 0.75 and 0.80 are both 0 days. Top-indicator percentiles: MVRV Z 42.2 / NUPL 42.5 / Puell 68.5 (10/13). The top zone requires any two ≥ 80.
200-day MA hedge: run 0 days, distance −11.5%. It needs 5 straight closes below 72,204 and cuts 20%.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs took in $175.7M on 10/13, October's second-largest inflow day; FBTC $103.1M, IBIT $65.9M, MSBT $6.7M
news.read: SoSoValue shows +$175.62M, less than 1% apart, so the site lists 10/13 as provisional. It is the largest single-day inflow since 10/07, but the seven complete days 10/02–10/12 still total −$556.7M and October is still net negative; it takes several straight inflow days to call a turn in flows. Realized cap +1.28% over 30 days agrees in direction. No change to market stage or exit framework.

news.title: Treasuries whipsawed after the hot CPI: the 10-year hit 5.3293% intraday, then closed down 2.7 bp at 5.19%; the 2-year closed at 4.802%. October hike odds rose from 22% to ~40%, easing to ~33% late (LSEG)
news.read: Yields giving back the spike shows markets still think the Fed is not in a hurry to move in October, while December hike bets firmed. Site FRED readings: 10-year 5.21%, real yield 2.88% (+28 bp over 20 days), so the high-rate backdrop is unchanged. With a BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation of 0.671, this drop mostly tracked equities. Short-term macro pressure; it does not touch the 200-day MA or any exit condition.

news.title: After CPI, BTC hit an intraday low near 81,500; $331M was liquidated across crypto in 24h, ~82% longs; BTC liquidations $69.95M
news.read: Smaller than the ~$489M on 10/12: a moderate long flush. Weighted funding on the site actually rose to 7.71% and the risk reversal firmed to −2.65, so leverage was not wiped out but is not crowded either; below sits a ~$303M Hyperliquid bid wall at 81,000. Short-term noise; it does not affect the cycle call.

news.title: US stocks closed lower after CPI: Nasdaq −1.9%, S&P 500 −1.0%, Dow −0.1%
news.read: Tech led the decline and BTC also closed near its daily low. With a BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation of 0.671, risk assets moving together is the recent theme; if equities keep falling, BTC will struggle to rally alone. This does not change the market stage above the 200-day MA.

news.title: NY Fed President Williams: one more hike may be appropriate this year, but he sees no need for further hikes in 2027; long-end yields eased
news.read: His signal is gentler than futures pricing (CME shows ~90% odds of a hike on 12/09) and helped Tuesday's BTC bounce, but the next day's hot CPI pushed October hike odds back up. The rate path is still a headwind and the site's 2.88% real yield is elevated: macro backdrop, not a framework condition.

news.title: Saylor told Bloomberg TV "we're at the beginning of a bull market" and said BTC bottomed slightly below $60,000; Strategy holds 848,250 BTC
news.read: Matches the direction of the site's rule-based Bull stage (since 10/09), but it is a holder's view, not data. The site's stage depends only on the 200-day MA and does not change on anyone's call.

news.title: Standard Chartered opened direct BTC and ETH trading from bank accounts to premium private clients in the UAE (unverified)
news.read: Single source, and its description of the regulator differs from September's institutional-launch coverage, so it is marked unverified. A long-run distribution story with no measurable effect on any site indicator.

research.summary: Glassnode's new 10/14 issue, Boxed In, sees BTC boxed between 80K–81.5K support (including the ETF cost basis near 81.5K) and 88K resistance. That matches the site's readings: a close near the 50-day MA and the 81,000 bid wall, with 7-day ETF flows still negative. K33's latest is still 10/12 (preview only); no new weekly from The Block Research or Coinbase Institutional in the last 7 days.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Boxed In
items.points: Cost basis of 6–12 month holders ~88K, of 1–2 year holders ~100K. True market mean ~78K (price above it since 9/18). US spot ETF cost basis ~81.5K; price dipped below it intraday on 10/08 and 10/13 and closed back above both times. ETF net inflows ~$3B over 9/21–10/06, ~−$760M since 10/07. Liquidation clusters just under 80K and near 88K.
items.meaning: Consistent with the site: the 81,576 close sits right on the ETF cost basis and the 81,000 bid wall. Its true market mean (~78K) and the site's bitcoin-data reading (79,248) come from different providers and are not subtracted; the site's supporting light uses its own series. Until 88K is reclaimed this is a range; no change to market stage or exit framework.

items.title: The Week On-chain: A Rally Running Light
items.points: Ask wall at 86.5K–86.75K, largest bid wall at 81K–81.25K; reclaiming 85.5K is needed for recovery. ~$4.9B of new capital over 30 days vs a $12.8B rise in realized cap; long-liquidation band 81.7K–83.3K, then 75K.
